25. See Dieter F. Uchtdorf, “ The Gift of Grace ,” Ensign or Liahona , May 2015, 107; see also Guide to the Scriptures, “ Grace ,” Gospel Library. I used to be confused by the many descriptions of God’s power found throughout the scriptures. They speak of grace as enabling power (see Philippians 4:13 ) but also the Light of Christ as power (see Doctrine and Covenant 88:13 ). We read of the power of faith (see Alma 18:35 ), the power of the Holy Ghost (see Moroni 10:7 ), and power from on high promised in temples (see Doctrine and Covenants 38:32 ; 105:11 ). Scriptures also teach of the power of the priesthood (see Doctrine and Covenants 113:8 ). I couldn’t figure out where one ended and the others began. Finally, I realized that “there is no other power, save the power of God” ( Doctrine and Covenants 8:7 ; see also Romans 13:1 ). Different labels for God’s power do not describe different powers but varying amounts, uses, and aspects of the same power.
